text:
linh: Heads-up — ACME cloud asked us to pin ROCm for their marketplace image. They saw regressions with 5.3 in their internal perf tests and want a certified image we can ship to the marketplace by next Tuesday.

carlos: Do we have a vetted ROCm 5.2 build that matches our kernel support matrix?

eva: We do have an internal `rocm-5.2` branch used for onprem customers, but it hasn’t gone through marketplace packaging. It’s currently built against kernel 5.15 and CUDA drivers omitted for ROCm-only nodes.

mike: Marketplace requirement: immutable AMI with pinned driver stack + manifest. They need the exact package hashes to run their signing process. Can we provide a reproducible image tag? Example: `redwood-runtime:rocm-5.2.1-20260321`

linh: Yes — we should create a hotfix branch `drivers/hotfix/rocm-5.2.1-marketplace` and cut an AMI. Need signoffs: eng-runtime (mike), eng-ml (anya) for perf, partnerships for announcement copy.

anya: I'll run a quick perf smoke: 1) end-to-end latency on typical chat workload, 2) memory regressions on KV cache hits, 3) sample quant kernel checks. ETA EOD tomorrow.

carlos: Also watch for kernel ABI mismatches. ACME is air-gapped for some SI customers; they will expect an offline bundle + install instructions. We should include `drivers.tar.gz` and post-install steps in `/opt/redwood/README.marketplace.md`.

vendor-ci-bot: build triggered: `hotfix/drivers/rocm-5.2.1` → artifact id `art-2026-03-21-56`

mike: Can someone own the canary rollout? Proposed lane: canary (ACME lab) -> regional marketplace (EU) -> global. Each step 24h with rollback window. I can own canary and rollback automation.

linh: Thanks. Partnerships will coordinate announcement timing with ACME marketing. Proposed public announcement no earlier than 48h after global rollout completes. Need legal to check joint branding line.

eva: Note: there was a subtle quant kernel reorder fix in our internal 5.2 patch. We should include the changelog entry: "Fix: quantized matmul reorder causing 0.02% score drift on long sequences" so customers are aware.

anya: Smoke result preview: latency +1.8% on median, p95 unchanged, memory unchanged for 8k KV cache. Flagging one regression in small-batch throughput on A100s — will attach perf logs.

carlos: If small-batch on A100 regresses, ACME will want fallback to compatible CUDA pipeline. Can we provide automatic fallback to our CUDA-compute variant in the customer routing policy?

mike: Yes — runtime already supports model-variant fallbacks. I’ll add a marketplace-aware route rule: `if hw==A100 && rocm_fallback_signaled then route: cuda-compatible` (will push rule to `marketplace-routes` repo).

linh: Action items: 1) mike cut hotfix AMI + OWN canary (assigned), 2) eva prepare changelog + offline bundle (assigned), 3) anya finish perf smoke + attach logs (assigned), 4) carlos draft install README and SI note (assigned), 5) partnerships coordinate announcement and legal check (linh).

mike: Starting AMI build now. Command: ```./scripts/make_ami.sh --stack rocm-5.2.1 --tag redwood-runtime:rocm-5.2.1-20260321 --output marketplace-ami-20260321```

vendor-ci-bot: ami pipeline passed basic tests → `ami-2026-03-21-78`

anya: Uploaded perf logs at https://internal.redwood/attachments/rocm-5.2.1-smoke.zip (ACME will get a read-only link).

carlos: Draft README pushed to `partnerships/marketplace/ACME/README.marketplace.md` — please review.

linh: Perfect. If we all hit these checks, partnerships will request ACME to start marketplace signing on Monday. Please react here with :thumbsup: when you have completed your assigned item.

mike: :thumbsup: (owning canary + rollback)

eva: :thumbsup: (changelog + bundle uploaded to artifacts)

carlos: :thumbsup: (README done)

anya: :thumbsup: (perf smoke complete, uploading final logs)

linh: Great. Leaving this thread open for any regression discoveries — tag @linh if you find anything critical.

vendor-ci-bot: scheduled follow-up test in 24h: `marketplace-smoke-post-canary`
